There are 2 worlds in this piece: one is barren, empty and dark. In there though is another, protected world inside the glass structure - a better world bright and full of life and color.

I know, I'm stating the obvious but it's for the sake of discussion...

Can't we say all humans are like this? We live in the world of today, which often can be hard and cruel. Our memories though carry our best moments - it's not that yesterday was better necessarily, just that in memory we can relieve all the good times and joys at once, whenever we want.

But isn't this image also a representation of innocence? Innocence is a fragile thing that we carry inside and if we allow that palace to break down and fade away then we'll have nothing else but the environment around us, at face value. Once your innocence shatters, can you ever reach that place again? How is it we can carry this fragile thing and keep it safe when the modern world is so violent and ruthless?

This image is so powerful because it plays with the duality of life: now and then, inside and outside, life and death... Everyone can relate to it in some way. Even though this is more abstract than Anxiety and I can't paint this is still a great visual representation of a human emotion - in this case the idea of having something beautiful and precious inside of us. I can absolutely relate and have added this piece to my wallpaper slideshow - thanks a lot OP!
